title: Robustness: Withdrawal as a Resolution Event
section_job: Probe the differential-timing result of Section 3.3, whose post bin is dated to completion (post-withdrawal quarters are dropped), so the peak-to-completion and gap-to-completion legs are estimated only over deals that complete. This is a within-sample selection on a post-treatment outcome, which deals complete. The peak-to-gap leg is exempt by construction, since the gap is the public announcement. As a supplementary check, let a withdrawal count as a resolution and re-estimate. The decline holds (residual peak-to-completion 0.0687, p<.01). Honesty: the resolution-inclusive sample adds only 89 firm-quarters and one firm (about 0.3 percent), so the decline can barely move and the check is low-powered; the load-bearing reassurance against selection is structural rather than statistical, namely the peak-to-gap leg, which never conditions on outcome.
spine: P1 the design property: the post bin is dated to completion, so the completion-reaching legs are estimated only over deals that complete (the peak-to-gap leg is exempt). P2 the supplementary check and its modest rationale: a withdrawal resolves the disclosure state too, so redefine the post bin to count any resolution and re-estimate. P3 result: the decline holds (peak-to-completion 0.0687 against 0.0723; peak-to-gap 0.0457 against 0.0455; cash 0.0204). P4 the honest bound: the sample adds only 89 firm-quarters and one firm (about 0.3 percent), so survival is near mechanical; the real reassurance is the structural peak-to-gap leg; read as consistent with the main specification, not as an independent test.

paragraphs.final_prose: The differential-timing result of Section~3.3 dates the post bin to completion: a deal's quarters enter the post bin only once it has closed, and the quarters that follow a withdrawal are dropped from the event clock. Two of the three contrasts that trace the round trip, the decline from the pre-announcement peak to completion and from the gap to completion, are therefore estimated only over deals that complete. Because completing and withdrawn deals need not be alike, part of the post-completion decline could in principle reflect which deals complete rather than the resolution of the disclosure state. The third contrast is not exposed to this: the decline from the pre-announcement peak to the gap is measured at the public announcement, a point every announced deal reaches whatever its eventual outcome, so it conditions on nothing that follows.

intent.statement: Run the supplementary check with a modest rationale. A withdrawal ends the disclosure state as surely as a completion does: once a pending deal is called off and disclosed, the executive is no longer answering around it. Redefine the post bin so that the quarters at and after a withdrawal enter it alongside the completed quarters, and re-estimate the Section 2.4 event study on this resolution-inclusive sample (point to the table). Folding in the withdrawn deals asks whether the post-resolution decline is particular to the deals that complete or appears whenever the disclosure state resolves. The framing is modest, not a strong claim that attenuation would prove an artifact; the power bound is paragraph four.

paragraphs.final_prose: We can probe the completion-dated legs directly by letting a withdrawal count as a resolution of the deal in the same way a completion does. A withdrawal ends the disclosure state as surely as a completion: once a pending deal is called off and disclosed, the executive is no longer answering around it. We therefore redefine the post bin so that the quarters at and after a withdrawal enter it alongside the completed quarters, and we re-estimate the event study of Section~2.4 on this resolution-inclusive sample; Table~\ref{tab:empire_drop_resolution} reports it. Folding in the withdrawn deals asks whether the post-resolution decline is particular to the deals that complete or appears whenever the disclosure state resolves.

intent.statement: Bound the check honestly and name the real reassurance. Few first deals are withdrawn and then observed for complete-case quarters within the post window, so the resolution-inclusive sample adds only 89 firm-quarters and one firm to the 28,102 of the main analysis; with so little new data the post-completion decline can barely move, so the result shows that the handful of withdrawn deals behave like the completed ones rather than ruling out a completion-driven reading on its own. The firmer ground is structural: the peak-to-gap leg is measured at announcement and conditions on nothing that follows, so the resolution of the residual at announcement never depended on which deals complete. Read as consistent with the main specification, not as an independent test.

paragraphs.final_prose: This check is a narrow one, and its main reassurance is structural rather than statistical. Few first deals are withdrawn and then observed for complete-case quarters within the post window, so the resolution-inclusive sample adds only $89$ firm-quarters and a single firm to the $28{,}102$ of the main analysis; with so little new data the post-completion decline can barely move, so the result shows that the handful of withdrawn deals behave like the completed ones rather than ruling out a completion-driven reading on its own. The firmer ground is the announcement-quarter leg itself: the decline from the pre-announcement peak to the gap is measured when the deal becomes public and conditions on nothing that follows, so the resolution of the residual at announcement never depended on which deals complete. We read the resolution-inclusive estimates as consistent with the main specification rather than as an independent test of it.
